social/avatar.notes: `initials(name)` returns the letters ("Ada Lovelace" → "AL", upper-cased for the current locale).
social/avatar.a11y:
`role="img"` with the name as its accessible name (`label` overrides it); the image and the initials are hidden, so
the name is read once. `decorative` hides the whole avatar when the name is written beside it. Text on the colour uses
the theme "on" tokens.

props: the "+N" bubble, or your own content in it
one colour for every avatar (a person's own wins)
social/avatar-group.a11y:
`role="group"` named with the number of people; each avatar is an image named after its person, the bubble reads
"+N". Margins are logical, so the overlap mirrors in right-to-left text.

"✓✓" : "✓"}} formatTime={(d) => d.toLocaleTimeString("en", { hour: "numeric" })} replyHint={false} tools={false} /> ``` Stable classes: `m-msg-bubble`, `m-msg-sender`, `m-msg-quote`, `m-msg-text`, `m-msg-meta`, `m-msg-edited`, `m-msg-tick`, `m-msg-reacts`, `m-msg-react`, `m-msg-retry`, `m-msg-tools`, `m-msg-tool-react`, `m-msg-tool-reply`, `m-msg-hint`.
social/chat-bubble.a11y:
Ticks are images named "Sent", "Read" …; reaction chips are buttons with `aria-pressed` named "❤️ 2". React and Reply
buttons appear on hover and keyboard focus, so drag-to-reply is never the only way.

nothing at 0 (a count next to an icon)
your own text for screen readers (default: the full grouped number)

social/count-roll.notes:
```tsx
<CountRoll value={$likes} formatter={(n) => `${n} likes`} duration={600} stagger={60} />
<CountRoll value={$likes} roll={false} />
```

`formatCount(n, format)` returns the same text without the element.
social/count-roll.a11y:
The rolling digits are `aria-hidden`; screen readers read the full value from a visually hidden copy. Inside a button
the count becomes part of the button's name.

social/follow-button.notes:
```tsx
<FollowButton state={$s} onChange={set} labels={{ follow: "Join", following: "Member" }} color="brand-green"
  icon={(s) => (s === "follow" ? <Icon of={star} /> : null)} burst={false} morph={false}
  ariaLabel={(s, name) => (s === "follow" ? `Join ${name}` : `Leave ${name}`)} />
```
social/follow-button.a11y:
A toggle button (`aria-pressed`) whose name says what pressing does: "Follow HADİ", "Following HADİ, press to
unfollow", "Follow request sent to HADİ, press to cancel".

props: the owner updates `liked` and the count (optimistic)
CountRoll next to the heart, hidden at 0
your own icon (a March glyph fills with the color while liked)
the pop of the icon on toggle
social/like-button.notes:
```tsx
<LikeButton liked={$on} onToggle={set} icon={<Icon of={star} />} color="brand-gold" label="Favourite"
  pop={false} burstOptions={{ count: 16, ring: false }} countFormat="full" />
```

`heartBurst(el, { count, radius, colors, ring })` and `heartPop(el, on)` (motion/burst.ts, re-exported here) are the same effects for any element: a
double-tap on a photo (PostCard), a comment, a story.
social/like-button.a11y:
A real `<button>` with `aria-pressed`; the count is part of its name. Space and Enter toggle it. The burst is
decorative (`aria-hidden`).

social/media-grid.a11y:
A group named "N photos"; every tile is a button named by its alt text and "Photo i of n". Keyboard activation opens
at once (no double-tap wait). The video mark and "+N" are decorative; "+N" is part of the count in the group name.

social/reply-quote.a11y:
The name and the text are plain text, read in order. With `onClick` they are one real button; the cancel button is a
separate button beside it (never nested) with its own name. The cut text stays whole for screen readers.

social/story-progress.a11y:
A `progressbar` named "Stories" whose value is read as the text "Story 2 of 5" (`aria-valuetext`; `aria-valuenow`
counts the finished segments, `aria-valuemax` all of them). The moving fill itself is not announced.

social/story-ring.a11y:
A button (or an image) named with the state: "HADİ, new story" / "HADİ, story seen". `aria-busy` while loading. The
ring and the badge are decorative.

social/verified-mark.a11y:
`role="img"` with the label as its name, so the name is read as "Deniz Kaya, Verified". With `label={false}` the badge
is `aria-hidden`; use that only when the text beside it already says the account is verified.
